- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to account for reversal bias.
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior period), reduce by 5–10% in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply slight upward bias to first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.33), model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of true outcome by 1–2 days in such cases.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
